question_text: Find the length of the chord intercepted by the circle x² + y² − x + 3y − 22 = 0 on the line y = x − 3.

insider_note: The line is given as y = x − 3, not in the ax + by + c = 0 form, so the first move is to rewrite it as x − y − 3 = 0 — using it as given is the commonest way to lose the distance mark here.
formula_note: Length of a chord uses 2√(r² − p²), with p the perpendicular distance from the centre to the LINE — different from the length of a tangent from an external POINT, which is √S₁₁, with no perpendicular distance involved. Confusing the two formulas is the usual slip between chord-length and tangent-length questions in this unit.

steps.label: Centre and radius
steps.margin_note: One mark. Both coefficients are odd, so g and f are halves and the radius comes out over √2.
steps.memory_tip: Odd coefficients give halves. Put everything over 4 before taking the square root.
steps.why: Comparing with the general form gives 2g = −1 and 2f = 3. Writing 22 as 88/4 puts every term over the same denominator, so the root is taken once.
common_mistakes: Taking g = −1 and f = 3 without halving.

steps.label: Perpendicular distance from the centre
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Rewrite y = x − 3 as x − y − 3 = 0 first; the coefficients are then 1 and −1.
steps.memory_tip: Move everything to one side before using the distance formula.
lines: Write the line as x − y − 3 = 0

lines.text: Distance from (x₁, y₁) to ax + by + c = 0 is

steps.why: The distance formula needs the line in the form ax + by + c = 0. Subtracting a negative y-coordinate is where the sign is usually lost: −(−3/2) is +3/2.
common_mistakes: Using y = x − 3 directly and taking a = 1, b = 1.
lines_compact: Write the line as x − y − 3 = 0

steps.label: Length of the chord
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Both r² and p² are halves, so they subtract cleanly before the root is taken.

lines.text: The radius, p and half the chord form a
right triangle, so half the chord

steps.why: Both squares are halves, so the subtraction is done before the root: 49/2 − 1/2 = 48/2 = 24. Then √24 = 2√6, and the factor 2 outside makes 4√6.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as 2√24 without taking out the perfect square 4.

steps.label: The picture
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own; the question does not ask for a diagram. The same picture serves every chord question.
steps.memory_tip: Radius, perpendicular distance and half the chord: a right-angled triangle every time.
steps.why: The perpendicular from C to the chord bisects it, so half the chord, p and r form a right-angled triangle. The formula 2√(r² − p²) is Pythagoras applied to that triangle and doubled.
common_mistakes: Placing the perpendicular from a point on the circle instead of from the centre.
Reading the answer as half the chord rather than the whole chord.
